course.title: Technology and Digital Transformation
course.description: This course examines the development of scientific ideas and engineering practices from early civilizations to the practice from early civilizations to the present day. Students will explore major discoveries, inventions and technological milestones. It provides students with a historical perspective to better understand modern engineering

clos.description: Analyse scientific and engineering developments through key historical discoveries and technologies.
Participate in teamwork and discussion on historical scientific and engineering advancement.
Demonstrate responsibility and active engagement in learning tasks and class activities.
Explain ethical issues related to scientific and technological developments and their impact.

contentRows: Topic 1: Introduction to Technology and Digital Transformation Meaning and scope of science and engineering in historical context Major stages in the development of science and engineering Importance of historical developments in shaping society and technology
Topic 2: The Scientific Revolution Key discoveries and major contributors during the Scientific Revolution Influence of the Scientific Revolution on later science and engineering

Topic 3: Historical Development of Modern Engineering and Technological Advancement Growth of modern engineering fields and major technologies Influence of past developments on modern engineering practices
Topic 4: Historical Case Study Topic selection with short explanation of each case Analysis of development, impact and limitations Influence of historical innovation on current technology

Topic 5: Ethical Issues in Historical Engineering and Technological Development Ethical principles in historical development of science and Ethical concern during major historical periods of technological growth Social and environmental impacts of past engineering and technological developments

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
